correctness.rationale: The gamma-ratio comparison bounds T[n,j] by C_s,α (n−j+1)^(s−1)/(n+1)^s. Applying Schur to weights (n+1)^−1/2 proves boundedness for s>0, α>−1. Triangularity cancels all entries within the first N+1 rows/columns in Tr(P_N (T*T−TT*) P_N), leaving exactly Σ_(n>N,j≤N)|T[n,j]|². Gamma-ratio asymptotics convert this cross-boundary sum to the double integral s²∫_(1)^∞∫_0^1 (x−y)^(2s−2)x^(−2s)dy dx. Tail O(1/R) and corner estimates O(eps^(2s)), O(eps log 1/eps), O(eps) in the three ranges protect the singular near-(1,1) boundary. The substitution u=y/x gives ∑_(k≥1)1/[k(k+2s−1)]; digamma evaluation includes the removable half-order π²/24. The exact Beta(1,s) Hausdorff representation at α=0 and classical bounded-Hausdorff subnormality (explicitly recalled in Ma Sec.1) imply D≥0, so finite diagonal sums establish genuine trace class. Independent finite flux approximations for five noninteger/integer s and several shifts remained below expected limiting constants, though finite truncations are not proof.
residual_risks: For α≠0, only the finite-section trace limit is asserted; trace-class status, hyponormality and trace norm are NOT concluded.
Use of classical Sharma subnormality for all bounded positive Hausdorff operators is a genuine external theorem; the beta measure is normalized and nonnegative for every s>0.

originality.rationale: Ma (2026) proves hyponormality of generalized Cesàro matrices only at positive integer orders. A separately inspected published exact harmonic trace formula covers all integer orders and shifts, and is explicitly PRIOR. The gamma interpolation to all real positive orders is not determined merely by those integer values; the present singular Riemann argument and shift-invariant flux across 0<s<1/2 are the surviving new statements. The subnormality of α=0 Hausdorff matrices is also classical prior input. The 2024 fractional Hausdorff factorization primary article could not be fully accessed and remains a qualified priority risk.

value.rationale: The canonical trace of a positive self-commutator and the finite-section boundary flux are meaningful operator invariants, and the fractional-order family is natural rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. An explicit all-real-order digamma formula, including its nontrivial s=1/2 removable regime, genuinely extends the known integer-order harmonic trace and exposes shift-independent boundary behavior.
residual_risks: The integer-order formula and unshifted subnormality are prior and supply no novel value alone.
No Schatten spectrum, shifted fractional trace norm or full shift trace class is determined.

final_claim: For every real order s>0 and shift α>−1, the finite-coordinate compression trace of D=T* T−T T* for the specified gamma-ratio lower-triangular generalized Cesàro operator tends to F(s)=s²(ψ(2s)+γ)/(2s−1), with continuous value π²/24 at s=1/2, independent of α. At α=0 positivity of bounded Hausdorff operators makes D trace class with true trace F(s).
limitations: s>0 and α>−1, with no uniformity in either parameter.
Only α=0 is established as trace class; at shifted α the limit is of finite-coordinate compressed traces, not full trace.
